reviews.title: Kinda Sus…
reviews.text:
Most of this I feel like could be learned in a chat with ChatGPT for free (not that I’d recommend that). A bit of a scam then.
Besides, increasing your intelligence is NOT done by having summaries read to you. There’s no shortcut to true intelligence…you have to read the book. Figure out what the author is trying to say and don’t rely on someone (or something) telling you what to think.

Some of the prompts had poor grammar too…didn’t make me trust this developer 😅. I looked at another app called “history” by the same developer, and it literally had the same question prompts asked as in this app when you open it.

Feels like a bit of a scam then…

reviews.title: Worth the Money if you like Books
reviews.text:
Pro: More than a preview for books you want to read or listen to in order to filter choices for buying books or audio books. 
Con: You can’t search titles. 

 I like this app, I’m on the free trial right now but I’m gonna go ahead and buy it. I don’t always have time to sit down and read or audiobook listen and when I do I hate finding myself halfway through a book or audiobook just to realize it’s not at all what I was looking for and feeing like I wasted my time and money. I buy at least 30 books a year; 10 audio 20 digital or hard copy. That’s around $150-$200 in books and for half of them to not be what I wanted I’m wasting $75-$100 per year. I’m hoping the summarizing app will make better use of the short chunks of time I have and help filter out the books I don’t want and with data analytics suggest more of what I do want, therefore better optimizing my book purchases. 

I just wish I could search by title/author or suggest a book for summarizing.
